topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The 45° scan range affects link budget calculations by introducing increased side lobe levels (SLLs) due to off-focus illumination, leading to more interference for edge-of-coverage users. This results in reduced capacity allocation for these users. The anisotropy of the corrugated waveguide exacerbates this effect on v-polarized beams. In contrast, broadside beams experience less interference and higher capacity allocation. The increased SLLs with 45° scan range result in reduced effective antenna gain for edge-of-coverage users, requiring increased transmit power or reduced capacity to maintain the same link budget.

These studies demonstrate the importance of considering scanning effects in link budget calculations, particularly for edge-of-coverage users.
